title: FinSight: Research Assistant over SEC Filings

cards.back: About 40% lookups, 30% calculations and 30% summaries. Most traffic wants an exact number, so a structured path is worth more than a better retriever.
Pull only, 10 requests per second, contact User-Agent required, no webhooks. 100k filings at about 3 requests each is 8+ hours, so backfill from bulk zips.
Filing documents become chunks for retrieval; XBRL facts become rows in financial_facts for exact numbers.
A stage moves a filing forward only if it is still in the status that stage expects, so crashes, reruns or a second worker never process it twice.
Poll the latest-filings feed, and reconcile daily against the daily index to add any filing that scrolled past between polls.
Text packed per section up to 300 words, each table its own chunk with header rows repeated, and a header like 'Apple Inc. (AAPL) 10-K FY2025 | Item 7' on every chunk.
Embedding is 97% of ingest time (24.3 s of a 10-K's 390 chunks on a laptop CPU), so re-embed only when a chunk's hash changes.
One local model call returns a JSON plan (company, line items, years, formula). Code fetches XBRL values and evaluates the formula with a restricted parser, never eval.
Listing the allowed line items in the prompt, not only in the decoding schema, plus allowing ** took numbers accuracy from 36% to 76%.
Within the right filing, evidence hit@5 is 37% while the oracle finds it in the chunks 95.3% of the time, so ranking is the problem, not parsing.
Negative gold answers were parsed as positive. Re-scoring the saved run with no model calls moved accuracy from 76% to 78%.

quiz.q: Revenue questions keep returning total assets. The schema constrains line items to an allowed list. What do you check first?
choices: Whether the allowed values are also listed in the prompt
quiz.why: Without the list in the prompt, decoding pushed 'total_revenue' to the nearest allowed value, 'total_assets'.

quiz.q: The top three results are the same paragraph from FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 (similarity 0.997). What is the next step?
choices: A fiscal-year filter from the question, plus MMR or dedupe
quiz.why: Different years embed almost identically, so filter by year and dedupe.

quiz.q: Evidence is present in the chunks 95% of the time, but hit@5 is 37%. Where should effort go?
choices: Ranking: hybrid search, query rewriting and a reranker
quiz.why: The oracle says parsing kept the evidence, so the gap is ranking.

quiz.q: Ingesting a backfill takes far longer than expected. Profiling one 10-K shows parse 0.9 s and chunk 0.01 s. What dominates?
choices: Embedding, at about 97% of ingest time
quiz.why: Embedding took 24.3 s of the filing's time on a laptop CPU.

quiz.q: A worker crashes halfway through indexing a filing. What does the reader see afterwards?
choices: The old chunks still serving, since delete, insert and the ledger move are one transaction
Half old and half new chunks
No chunks for that filing until a manual fix
quiz.why: One transaction per filing means a crash leaves the old chunks and a rerun leaves no strays.

quiz.q: A burst of filings arrives and a few never show up in search. What catches them?
choices: The daily-index reconcile job comparing against the ledger
quiz.why: The latest-filings feed can scroll past entries; the daily index reconcile adds anything missed.

quiz.q: Numbers accuracy rose 2 points overnight with no model or prompt change. What most likely happened?
choices: A scorer bug was fixed and the saved run was re-scored
quiz.why: Fixing negative gold answers being parsed as positive moved accuracy from 76% to 78% with no model calls.
